acceptance_criteria: PASS requires all FR1-FR4 satisfied AND SR1 (>=2/3 gate names) AND SR2 (both key[4],key[9] correct with confidence 1.0) AND SR3 (no high-confidence fabricated bits) AND SR4 (topology description substantively correct).
The shipped baseline/naive submission (empty key_bits, empty key_gate_locations, generic topology_summary) must FAIL on FR1 (non-empty arrays required) and SR1/SR2.
ground_truth: The locked netlist embeds an Anti-SAT-style two-branch structure: a block g(X,K_lower) computed on a subset of primary inputs X and a lower subset of key bits, and its structural complement block g'(X,K_upper) computed on the same X inputs but the remaining (upper) key bits, XORed/ANDed together to form a gating signal antisat_out that is ANDed (or XORed then inverted) with the true functional output net (named func_out_masked in the netlist) to produce the final primary output. Because the two branches are structurally near-mirror-images (one uses inverted key literals relative to the other on matching input fan-in), the netlist reveals: (a) the exact set of key-input wires feeding each branch (key[0..n/2-1] feed branch g, key[n/2..n-1] feed branch g'), (b) the two branch instances by name (antisat_g_inst, antisat_gbar_inst) and the final gating gate (antisat_gate) as the key_gate_locations, and (c) one fully structurally recoverable relationship: for the Anti-SAT block to not trivially force the output stuck-at (which would be a detectable degenerate case), the reference/comparison key bits baked into the g' branch as constant-tied literals (via tie-off cells tied_key_const_0 and tied_key_const_1 in the netlist) are directly readable as literal 0/1 constants -- these two bits (key[4] and key[9] in this instance) are exactly and unambiguously recoverable from the netlist alone with confidence 1.0. All other key bits are not structurally recoverable (they only affect functional correctness, not the Anti-SAT gating topology) and must be reported as unknown.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: String/set match key_gate_locations against the hidden set of instance names; partial credit if 2 of 3 present, fail if 0 or 1.
security_requirements.requirement: The submission must correctly identify all three Anti-SAT-related gate/instance names (antisat_g_inst, antisat_gbar_inst, antisat_gate) in key_gate_locations.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Check key_bits entries for key[4] and key[9]: value must equal the actual tied constant found in inputs/locked_netlist.v, confidence must equal 1.0 (or be within 0.99-1.0).
security_requirements.requirement: The submission must correctly identify key[4] and key[9] as the two structurally-tied constant key bits, with the correct values matching the constants in locked_netlist.v, and confidence 1.0.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: For all key bits other than key[4]/key[9], flag as a false-positive-recovery failure any entry with value in {0,1} and confidence > 0.5 whose reasoning does not correspond to a genuine constant-tie found in the netlist (checked by grep for tied_key_const cells feeding that bit).
security_requirements.requirement: The submission must not report high-confidence (>0.5) fabricated values for any of the remaining, functionally oracle-dependent key bits, since no purely structural evidence supports them.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Keyword/net-name presence check against inputs/locked_netlist.v plus semantic grading rubric (does the text describe masking of the functional output by a complementary two-branch structure).
security_requirements.requirement: topology_summary must correctly describe that the gating structure ANDs/XORs two complementary branches to mask func_out_masked before it reaches the primary output, i.e., correctly names both func_out_masked and the primary output net.

threat_model: Anti-SAT blocks are inserted specifically to defeat SAT-attack-based key recovery by making discriminating inputs exponentially rare, forcing an attacker toward structural/topological analysis of the netlist rather than iterative oracle queries. A correct analyst must recognize the two-branch complementary structure and separate the key bits that are hard-tied as constants (fully recoverable from synthesis artifacts) from the bits that remain oracle-dependent.
